entries.title: Meta ads for a Chembur housing developer

fields.title: Meta ads for a Chembur housing developer
fields.summary: A Chembur developer needed enquiries from people interested in its project, not Chembur property in general. We changed its Meta ads to focus on the project’s lifestyle.

content.value: The challenge was relevance, not volume
Om Sai Developer needed to sell its available 2 and 3 BHK apartments in Chembur, Mumbai, against a very specific buyer brief.
A much smaller market than Chembur as a whole
: The developer’s buyer brief, and the project’s lifestyle positioning, significantly narrowed the potential audience compared with the wider Chembur property market.
More enquiries alone would not solve it
: The task was not simply to generate more property enquiries. It was to find relevant prospective buyers within a much smaller audience.
Broad marketing could miss the right buyers
: Broad real-estate marketing could generate plenty of enquiries without necessarily reaching the people the developer was looking for.
The risk: wasted spend and sales time
: That could mean wasted marketing spend, irrelevant enquiries, and a sales team spending its time on prospects who were unlikely to move forward.
Make the ads about the project’s lifestyle, not just the property
Our insight:
the biggest challenge was not a lack of potential homebuyers in Chembur, but reaching the right people within a very narrow buyer profile.
Relevance over reach

: Broad real-estate advertising would have reached a much larger audience, many of whom would not have matched the developer’s requirements. So we focused the campaign on finding relevant prospective buyers while keeping wasted reach and irrelevant enquiries as low as possible.
Lifestyle-led creative instead of broad property ads
: We changed the Meta campaign from broad property advertising to creative and messaging that reflected the lifestyle the project wanted to represent.
A more focused message
: The creative and messaging were built around the project and its lifestyle positioning, which gave the campaign a more focused message than broad property advertising.
Lower cost per lead and more qualified leads
The reported before-and-after figures show a lower cost per lead and more qualified leads.
: cost per lead, a 90.27% reduction. Reported before-and-after comparison.
: qualified leads, a 209.1% increase. Reported before-and-after comparison.
More time with relevant prospective buyers
: the sales team could spend less time filtering through enquiries that were unlikely to move forward.
Relevance, not just volume
: Instead of attracting a large number of general property enquiries, the campaign brought in more qualified prospects who connected with the project’s lifestyle positioning.
More qualified leads, at a lower cost per lead
: The developer was getting more qualified leads while the cost of generating each lead fell.
Campaign-wide totals, 12 September 2024 to 28 February 2026
These totals cover the whole campaign. They are not part of the before-and-after comparisons above.
: advertising spend.
: total reported leads.

Give people a reason to enrol:

Measure purchases:

Work on the ads and the page together
We managed Google Search and Display campaigns with direct course purchases as the objective. The work covered both how people reached the website and the pages they saw after clicking.
Keyword changes:
We revised the keywords used in the campaigns to support the course-purchase objective.

We changed the ads and targeting to improve how the learning offer was presented to potential students.
Landing page changes:
We changed the landing pages as part of the same campaign effort, rather than treating the ad click as the end of the journey.

entries.title: Adapting course advertising as learning preferences changed

fields.title: Adapting course advertising as learning preferences changed
fields.summary: MappedSkills has worked on AnybodyCanBake’s Meta advertising since 2018. When demand shifted back towards offline learning after COVID, approaches that had worked for online courses became less effective. Course price revisions and expansion into international markets helped the business return to profitability, according to MappedSkills founder Amit Gupta. For September 2021 to October 2026, the business reports 3,892 paid enrolments attributed to Facebook Ads and ₹2,78,95,678 in revenue on ₹42,78,961 in advertising spend.

content.value: What worked earlier stopped working as well

Amit describes a learning market that moved from offline towards online courses, swung back towards offline learning after COVID, and is now seeing renewed interest in online learning. For AnybodyCanBake, the shift back towards offline demand affected advertising economics and profitability.
Changing customer preference:
Selling an online learning offer became harder when more prospective learners preferred an offline experience.
Pressure on profitability:
Continuing with an approach that had worked earlier was no longer enough to maintain profitable acquisition.
The objective stayed the same:
The campaigns remained focused on sales. The response needed to address the commercial offer and the markets reached.
Revisit pricing and reach beyond the existing market

The response combined course price revisions with expansion of sales advertising into international locations. It addressed both the value of a sale and the markets in which the offer could find buyers.
Course price revisions:
Pricing was revised as part of the response to weaker advertising economics. Course names, prices and individual offers are not disclosed.
International expansion:
The advertising reach expanded into international locations, opening the offer to learners beyond the existing market.
Sales remained the focus:
The campaigns continued to pursue purchases through changing market conditions rather than changing the success measure to clicks or views.
3,892 paid enrolments and ₹2 crore 79 lakh in reported revenue
From September 2021 to October 2026, the reported totals show 3,892 paid enrolments attributed to Facebook Ads and ₹2,78,95,678 in revenue. The corresponding advertising spend was ₹42,78,961.
return on ad spend. Approximately ₹6.52 in reported revenue per ₹1 of advertising spend, calculated from the whole-period totals, September 2021 to October 2026. ROAS alone does not establish profit.

in reported revenue, approximately ₹2.79 crore, across September 2021 to October 2026.
in advertising spend across September 2021 to October 2026.
advertising cost per paid enrolment. Advertising spend divided by paid enrolments, calculated from the whole-period totals.
A return to profitability with continued adaptation

Amit reports that price revisions and international expansion helped restore profitability. The engagement continues as online learning interest picks up again. These aggregate figures do not imply that results improved every month or that every phase was profitable.

fields.evidenceNote: The relationship history, market observations, sales-campaign objective, commercial changes and results were supplied by MappedSkills founder Amit Gupta. fields.title: 874 attributed orders from Meta Ads at ₹411.90 per order
fields.summary: For Advit Prints, the campaign connected visual product discovery with measurable orders. Advertising spend of ₹3,60,000 generated 874 attributed orders and ₹11,36,200 in attributed revenue, a 3.16× revenue return on ad spend.

content.value: Handblock prints need more than an attractive product shot. Buyers want to understand the fabric, finish and how a piece will look in use. The challenge was to communicate those details clearly enough to move from interest to purchase.
Show the product in use.
Combine fabric closeups with styling and home use scenes to make the product easier to evaluate.
Match creative to buying stage.
Give new audiences a clear introduction and use relevant product reminders for eligible returning visitors.
Keep the campaign focused on orders.
Review creative through purchase cost and order value, supported by catalogue availability and purchase tracking.
874 attributed orders and ₹11,36,200 in attributed order revenue

The campaign delivered an average attributed order value of ₹1,300 against an acquisition cost of ₹411.90 per order. That places the commercial story around purchases and revenue efficiency, rather than clicks or engagement.

For a visual textile brand, show the details that help a customer decide and measure the result at purchase level.

fields.evidenceNote: The figures and the month range were supplied by MappedSkills in the final case study set of 30 October 2026. Cost per order is ₹3,60,000 divided by 874. Average order value is ₹11,36,200 divided by 874. Revenue ROAS is ₹11,36,200 divided by ₹3,60,000. The month range does not establish exact day boundaries. Attribution settings, refund treatment, product margins and the share of repeat buyers were not supplied, and revenue return is not profit. The figures have not been independently checked against account exports and order records.

entries.title: 27 signed engagements from Google Ads at ₹13,333.33 each

fields.title: 27 signed engagements from Google Ads at ₹13,333.33 each
fields.summary: Meticulous Business Plan generated 287 enquiries through Google Ads, of which 94 were qualified and 27 became signed engagements. With ₹3,60,000 in advertising spend and ₹12,15,000 in engagement revenue, the campaign delivered 3.38× revenue ROAS.

content.value: Someone searching for a business plan may want a free template, academic help or a paid consulting engagement. The challenge was to reach businesses ready to commission work and judge performance by the quality of the resulting pipeline.
Focus on commercial service intent.
Separate business plan and project report searches into focused campaign themes.
Reduce irrelevant enquiries.
Review search terms for free template, academic and unrelated research intent, and align the landing page with the service searched.
Follow leads through to signed work.
Use enquiry qualification and engagement outcomes to assess the campaign beyond lead volume.
27 signed engagements from 287 enquiries
Of 287 unique enquiries, 94 were qualified and 27 became signed engagements. Advertising spend of ₹3,60,000 worked out at ₹1,254.36 per enquiry and ₹13,333.33 per signed engagement.

revenue return on ad spend. Revenue from engagements divided by advertising spend. Revenue return is not profit.

32.75% of enquiries qualified, and 28.72% of qualified enquiries became signed engagements. Across all enquiries, the conversion rate to signed work was 9.41%. The average revenue per signed engagement was ₹45,000. These are ratios of period totals, not a tracked cohort.
₹45,000 is revenue per engagement, not acquisition cost. The acquisition cost was ₹13,333.33, making signed work the most useful result to lead with.

fields.evidenceNote: The figures and the month range were supplied by MappedSkills in the final case study set of 30 October 2026. Costs and percentages are calculated from the supplied counts and rounded to two decimal places: cost per enquiry ₹3,60,000 divided by 287, cost per signed engagement ₹3,60,000 divided by 27, revenue ROAS ₹12,15,000 divided by ₹3,60,000. The enquiry, qualification and signing totals are period totals, so the rate of enquiries that became signed work is a period ratio, not a tracked cohort. The qualification criteria, the signing date basis and the attribution method were not supplied, and revenue return is not profit. The figures have not been independently checked against account exports and the client’s records.

entries.title: 540 new paid memberships at ₹400 per member

fields.title: 540 new paid memberships at ₹400 per member
fields.summary: Libros Library generated 2,204 membership enquiries and acquired 540 new paid memberships through Meta Ads. Advertising spend of ₹2,16,000 translated into ₹400 per new member. The supplied lifetime value is ₹4,800 per membership.

content.value: A subscription library asks customers to build an ongoing reading habit. The campaign needed to explain the value of membership clearly to customers of an online library serving readers across India.
Make the membership easy to understand.
Build creative around reading routines, book selection and membership convenience.
Describe the library accurately.
Present Libros Library as an online library serving customers across India.
Measure paid membership separately.
Follow the journey from enquiry to first paid membership so lead volume does not become the only measure of success.
540 new paid memberships from 2,204 enquiries
Advertising spend of ₹2,16,000 worked out at ₹98.00 per membership enquiry and ₹400.00 per new paid member.
new paid memberships, June 2025 to March 2026.
cost per new paid member. Advertising spend divided by new paid memberships.
of enquiries became paid memberships. 540 divided by 2,204, a ratio of period totals rather than a tracked cohort.

lifetime value per membership, as supplied. This is not revenue collected during the campaign and is not part of any return on ad spend.

At ₹400 in advertising cost per new member, the acquisition cost was one twelfth of the supplied ₹4,800 lifetime value. That comparison explains why recurring membership economics matter; lifetime value is not revenue collected during the campaign.
Lead with member acquisition cost and the value of an ongoing membership. Keep lifetime value separate from campaign revenue and ROAS.

fields.evidenceNote: The figures and the month range were supplied by MappedSkills in the final case study set of 30 October 2026. Cost per enquiry is ₹2,16,000 divided by 2,204, cost per new member ₹2,16,000 divided by 540, and the enquiry to membership rate is 540 divided by 2,204. The ₹4,800 lifetime value per membership is a supplied figure with no method or horizon supplied. It is not multiplied by the number of memberships, is not presented as revenue and is not used to compute a revenue return. Initial membership revenue was not supplied, so no revenue ROAS is shown. The enquiry and membership totals are period totals, not a tracked cohort. The figures have not been independently checked against account exports and membership records.

entries.title: 627 paid enrolments from learners searching for baking education

fields.title: 627 paid enrolments from learners searching for baking education
fields.summary: Bakedemy’s Google Ads campaign generated 5,620 course enquiries and 627 paid enrolments. Advertising spend of ₹24,00,000 supported ₹94,05,000 in attributed enrolment revenue, with a cost per enrolment of ₹3,827.75 and 3.92× revenue ROAS.

content.value: People comparing baking courses have different learning goals, budgets and preferred formats. The challenge was to connect serious learning intent with a relevant enquiry journey and follow that interest through to paid admission.
Organise campaigns around learning intent.
Match search themes and ad messages to the learner’s needs without exposing private course details.
Keep the landing journey relevant.
Use focused landing pages and filter irrelevant recipe, job and free content searches through search term review.
Measure admissions beyond enquiries.
Track enquiries and paid enrolments as separate stages, with admission outcomes informing performance reporting.
627 paid enrolments from 5,620 course enquiries
Advertising spend of ₹24,00,000 worked out at ₹427.05 per course enquiry and ₹3,827.75 per paid enrolment.

11.16% of enquiries became paid enrolments. Average attributed revenue per enrolment was ₹15,000. The case connects relevant search demand with admissions, giving prospective education clients a clear view of both lead cost and enrolment cost. These are ratios of period totals, not a tracked cohort.
A course enquiry matters most when it leads to the right learner joining. Report the admissions outcome alongside enquiry volume.

fields.evidenceNote: The figures and the month range were supplied by MappedSkills in the final case study set of 30 October 2026. Cost per enquiry is ₹24,00,000 divided by 5,620, cost per enrolment ₹24,00,000 divided by 627 and revenue ROAS ₹94,05,000 divided by ₹24,00,000. entries.title: 738 paid enrolments by turning baking interest into learning intent

fields.summary: Bakedemy’s Meta Ads activity generated 4,800 course enquiries and 738 paid enrolments. Advertising spend of ₹27,00,000 produced ₹1,10,70,000 in attributed enrolment revenue, with ₹3,658.54 cost per enrolment and 4.10× revenue ROAS.

content.value: Enjoying baking content does not automatically mean someone is ready to join a course. The challenge was to explain the learning offer, qualify interest and move suitable learners towards paid enrolment.
Let teaching introduce the offer.
Use instructor demonstrations, learning outcome explanations and approved learner stories to show the experience.
Match the message to readiness.
Give new audiences a clear introduction and use relevant follow up creative for eligible warm audiences.
Assess the result at enrolment level.
Follow enquiries through to paid admissions rather than treating lead generation as the final outcome.
738 paid enrolments from 4,800 course enquiries
Advertising spend of ₹27,00,000 worked out at ₹562.50 per course enquiry and ₹3,658.54 per paid enrolment.

entries.title: 6 signed design projects from Google Ads

fields.title: 6 signed design projects from Google Ads
fields.summary: Bblewrap generated 348 project enquiries, including 42 qualified design briefs and six signed projects. Advertising spend of ₹4,40,000 supported ₹12,00,000 in project revenue, resulting in ₹73,333.33 per signed project and 2.73× revenue ROAS.

content.value: Design searches attract different audiences, including businesses, students and jobseekers. The challenge was to reach businesses with a genuine design requirement and assess the resulting enquiries by brief quality and signed work.
Separate branding and package design intent.
Match search themes to the specific service a prospective client needs.
Make the portfolio support qualification.
Connect service focused enquiries with relevant work examples and clear project requirements.
Follow briefs through to signed projects.
Review lead quality alongside acquisition cost, keeping project enquiries and signed work distinct.
6 signed design projects from 348 enquiries
Of 348 unique project enquiries, 42 were qualified design briefs and 6 became signed projects. Advertising spend of ₹4,40,000 worked out at ₹1,264.37 per enquiry and ₹73,333.33 per signed project.

That is distinct from the ₹73,333.33 advertising cost to acquire each signed project. These are ratios of period totals, not a tracked cohort.
For a design consultancy, the strongest story is the work won from qualified briefs. Enquiry volume alone does not show commercial value.

fields.evidenceNote: The figures and the month range were supplied by MappedSkills in the final case study set of 30 October 2026. content.value: An enquiry for a professional service can be an information request or a business ready to appoint an adviser. The challenge was to connect relevant search demand with qualified consultations and paid work.
Keep service intent clear.
Structure search themes around the professional service the potential client needs.
Align the enquiry journey.
Use relevant landing page information and qualification questions to make the next step clear.
Report the commercial outcome.
Follow enquiries through qualified consultations and signed engagements, keeping each stage visible in reporting.
19 signed engagements from 580 enquiries

Of 580 unique enquiries, 127 led to qualified consultations and 19 became signed engagements. Advertising spend of ₹1,80,000 (INR equivalent) worked out at ₹310.34 per enquiry and ₹9,473.68 per signed engagement.

entries.title: 6,607 attributed orders and 3.12× revenue ROAS from Meta Ads

fields.title: 6,607 attributed orders and 3.12× revenue ROAS from Meta Ads
fields.summary: From April to September 2026, Wanderlooms generated 6,607 attributed orders and ₹1,12,32,000 in attributed revenue from ₹36,00,000 in Meta advertising spend. Cost per attributed order was ₹544.88, with average attributed order value of ₹1,700.02 and revenue ROAS of 3.12×.

content.value: Adventure apparel buyers need to understand style, fit and use before buying from a brand discovered through social media. The campaign needed to connect compelling product discovery with a clear purchase journey and measurable acquisition economics.
Showed the products in use.
We used outdoor lifestyle scenes, product details and fit demonstrations to help shoppers evaluate the offer.
Matched messages to purchase readiness.
We distinguished new audience discovery from relevant follow up to eligible visitors, keeping the message connected to where the shopper was in the buying journey.
Measured purchase efficiency.
We reviewed order acquisition cost, attributed order value and revenue, alongside product availability and returns, to keep reporting focused on commercial outcomes.
6,607 attributed orders and ₹1,12,32,000 in attributed order revenue
The campaign generated ₹3.12 in attributed revenue for every ₹1 spent on Meta advertising. Average attributed order value was ₹1,700.02 against an advertising acquisition cost of ₹544.88 per order.
